title: The inertia component of an equivariant product with purely inseparable residues
statement: Let $G$ be a finite group acting by ring automorphisms on a commutative ring $S$. For $H\leq G$ write $S^H=\{s:h(s)=s\text{ for all }h\in H\}$ and put $B=S^G$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be prime. Suppose $S\simeq\prod_{j=1}^n S_j$, $n\geq1$, is a product decomposition with corresponding orthogonal idempotents $e_j$, and $G$ permutes the $e_j$ and hence the factors. Suppose each factor has exactly one prime over $\mathfrak p$, corresponding to $\mathfrak Q_j\subset S$, and each field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak Q_j)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is purely inseparable (in characteristic $p>0$, every element $x$ satisfies $x^{p^m}\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for some $m\geq0$, or the extension is trivial in characteristic zero). Here $\kappa(Q)=\operatorname{Frac}(S/Q)$, and similarly for $B$. Put $I=\{g:g\mathfrak Q_1=\mathfrak Q_1,\ g|_{\kappa(\mathfrak Q_1)}=1\}$. Then $G$ is transitive on the factors, and $I$ is both the stabilizer of $\mathfrak Q_1$ and the stabilizer of $e_1$. Projection induces a $B$-algebra isomorphism $B=S^G\simeq(e_1S)^I$. For any representatives $g_jI$ sending $e_1$ to $e_j$, with $g_1=1$, its inverse sends $a\in(e_1S)^I$ to $\sum_jg_j(a)\in S^G$; this value is independent of the representatives. Moreover projection gives $S^I\simeq(e_1S)^I\times((1-e_1)S)^I$. The first factor defines an open and closed subscheme $W\subset\operatorname{Spec}S^I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-open-immersion] containing $\mathfrak Q_1\cap S^I$, and the structural morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an isomorphism. No faithfulness, Noetherian or group-order-invertibility hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-finite-invariant-prime-orbits-residues] with $H=G$, $D=S$, $A=B$: all $\mathfrak Q_j$ contract to $\mathfrak p$, so for each $j$ there is $g_j$ with $g_j\mathfrak Q_1=\mathfrak Q_j$. A prime belonging to factor $j$ contains every $e_k$ for $k\ne j$ and does not contain $e_j$: their images are orthogonal idempotents summing to one in a domain. Because $G$ permutes the $e_k$, the equality of primes forces $g_j(e_1)=e_j$. Thus the action on factors is transitive. Conversely, any $g$ fixing $e_1$ sends $\mathfrak Q_1$ to a prime in that factor over $\mathfrak p$ (it fixes $B$), hence fixes $\mathfrak Q_1$ by the assumed uniqueness. This also proves equality of the prime and factor stabilizers.

Let $D$ denote this common stabilizer. Since $g\in D$ preserves $\mathfrak Q_1$, its ring automorphism descends to $S/\mathfrak Q_1$ and then acts on fractions by $u/v\mapsto g(u)/g(v)$. It fixes $B$ pointwise, so this is a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-automorphism of $L=\kappa(\mathfrak Q_1)$. In characteristic $p>0$, for $x\in L$ choose $m$ with $x^{p^m}\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Then $(g(x)-x)^{p^m}=g(x^{p^m})-x^{p^m}=0$, so $g(x)=x$ since $L$ is a field. In characteristic zero the extension is trivial. Thus $D\subseteq I$, and $I\subseteq D$ holds by definition, proving $I=D$. The elements sending $e_1$ to $e_j$ are exactly the left coset $g_jI$: $g(e_1)=g_j(e_1)$ is equivalent to $g_j^{-1}g\in I$. Choose $g_1=1$.

For $a\in(e_1S)^I$ put $T(a)=\sum_jg_j(a)$. Replacing $g_j$ by $g_ji$ with $i\in I$ changes no summand. For $h\in G$, write $hg_j=g_{h\cdot j}i_j$ with $i_j\in I$; the preceding coset description gives this equality. Hence $hT(a)=\sum_jg_{h\cdot j}(a)=T(a)$, because $j\mapsto h\cdot j$ is a permutation. Thus $T(a)\in B$. Each $g_j(a)$ belongs to $e_jS$, so orthogonality gives $e_1T(a)=a$.

Projection $P:B\to(e_1S)^I$, $b\mapsto e_1b$, is well defined because $I$ fixes both $e_1$ and $b$. It preserves addition and multiplication and sends $1$ to the identity $e_1$ of $e_1S$. For $b\in B$, $T(P(b))=\sum_jg_j(e_1b)=\sum_je_jb=b$, while the preceding step gives $P(T(a))=a$. Thus $P$ is a ring isomorphism with inverse $T$. Give $(e_1S)^I$ its structural $B$-action $b\mapsto e_1b$; then $P$ and its inverse are $B$-linear, proving the claimed $B$-algebra isomorphism.

Since $I$ fixes $e_1$ and $1-e_1$, the map $s\mapsto(e_1s,(1-e_1)s)$ restricts to $S^I\to(e_1S)^I\times((1-e_1)S)^I$. Its inverse is $(a,c)\mapsto a+c$: this sum is $I$-fixed, its projections are $a,c$, and $e_1s+(1-e_1)s=s$. Orthogonality proves multiplication is preserved, and the identities correspond. This proves the stated product decomposition, with the first projection exactly multiplication by $e_1$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to the two rings $(e_1S)^I$ and $((1-e_1)S)^I$, using the preceding ring isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] its first coprojection identifies $W=\operatorname{Spec}((e_1S)^I)$ with an open and closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}S^I$. Its map is the spectrum of the first projection. More explicitly, the image is $D(e_1)$: in the product the idempotent $e_1$ is $(1,0)$, so a prime from the first spectrum omits it and a prime from the second contains it. Since $e_1\in S^I$ and $e_1\notin\mathfrak Q_1$, this open component contains $\mathfrak Q_1\cap S^I$. The structural map from $W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}P$, by composition of the inclusion $B\to S^I$ with this projection. By functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(P^{-1})$ is its inverse. This gives the asserted isomorphism over $B$.
